subject: Module stewardship and deployment catalog for private deployment
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@orchidsys.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Steve Huang <steve.huang@orchidsys.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Module stewardship and deployment catalog for private deployment

Jordan —

Thanks for taking this call last week. Orchid Systems is moving into PoC with a Fortune 500 customer and they require an on-prem package that maps ownership for Terraform/Helm/Ansible modules, plus a recommended deployment catalog that shows which modules are required for typical topologies (single-tenant VPC, hybrid VLAN, air-gapped on-prem). Their security team is specifically asking for:

- A clear module ownership matrix (who owns TF module, who maintains Helm charts, who runs Ansible runbooks)
- CI/CD gating recommendations and a minimal test matrix for infra changes
- Network segmentation patterns and a canonical deployment catalog we can include in our SOW

I attached a short requirements summary (initial_requirements_orchid.pdf) — can your team put together a short stewardship template and a draft catalog we can review? Ideally we'd have a 60–90 minute workshop with your infra leads this week or next to align on module boundaries and the GitOps flow.

Proposed workshop attendees from Orchid: myself, Steve Huang (netops), and their security reviewer (TBD). From Redwood we'd like module owners and whoever owns the private deploy CI gating.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Sr. Platform Architect
Orchid Systems

---
Attachment: initial_requirements_orchid.pdf (summary, 2 pages)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@orchidsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Module stewardship and deployment catalog for private deployment

Alex —

Appreciate the detail and the PDF, this is exactly the kind of ask we expect for our Private offering. I've attached a lightweight stewardship template (iac-stewardship-template.xlsx) and a short example catalog (deployment-catalog-examples.md) that shows one way to structure the mapping.

Quick answers / plan:
- We can run a 75-minute workshop to align on module boundaries, expected SLAs, and GitOps gates. I propose Tue/Wed next week 10–11:15 PT.
- Preliminary internal owners: Marissa will lead Terraform module design and vet naming conventions; Irene will own Helm chart versioning and release gating; I'll own overall deployment patterns and customer-facing catalog docs.
- Deliverables after the workshop: populated stewardship template, a draft deployment catalog with topology examples, and a CI gating checklist for your security team.

Please confirm a workshop slot that works for you and any additional attendees from the security side. If you can share the customer's expected topology (single-rack, multi-rack, VLAN requirements) we can pre-fill some examples.

Jordan Blake
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: iac-stewardship-template.xlsx, deployment-catalog-examples.md

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: draft module ownership and gating (do not forward)

Jordan / Irene —

Following up on Jordan's reply to Orchid. I've put together a draft ownership CSV and a short CI gating checklist. High-level notes inline:

1) Ownership matrix (attached module_ownership_draft.csv) — columns: module_name, terraform_owner, helm_owner, ansible_owner, public_contract, required_for_topologies
   - Suggest we mark three modules as "Redwood core-owned": network-base, kvcache, inference-runtime. These are maintained by infra-runtime team (we should confirm an owner in the runtime org).
   - Customer-specific modules (vlan-bridge, airgap-config) should be labeled partner-maintained with Redwood support SLAs.

2) CI gating checklist (summary):
   - TF plan in isolated test account + drift check
   - Helm chart lint + template rendering against k8s 1.26 cluster matrix
   - Ansible idempotence run against a staging VM image (minimal smoke tests)
   - Automated integration test: deploy minimal stack + run a tracer job to validate KV cache persistence

3) Deployment catalog approach:
   - We'll publish a canonical catalog (read-only) in the Private Deploy docs and produce a per-customer manifest that selects modules and parameter presets.
   - Include a network segmentation appendix with CIDR examples, firewall rules, and recommended NAT/egress patterns for compliance customers.

Open questions for the workshop:
- Where do we draw the line on owning customer network modules vs. providing prescriptive patterns?
- What SLA/response times do we promise for partner-maintained modules?
- Should we require a security sign-off from the customer's SecOps for any module flagged as "high-risk" before promoted to PROD?

Action: I've attached the draft CSV for your review. If you agree with the plan I can convert the checklist into a templated GitHub Actions pipeline (PR template) we can show to Orchid during the workshop.

Marissa Cole
Engineering Manager, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: module_ownership_draft.csv (preview: network-base,terraform-runtime-team,helm-runtime-team,ansible-runtime-team,public,true)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@orchidsys.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Steve Huang <steve.huang@orchidsys.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 00:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Module stewardship and deployment catalog for private deployment

Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks, that all looks good. Tue 2026-11-09 10:00 PT works for Orchid — please send a calendar invite and the pre-read. Security will want the gating checklist and the network appendix in advance; I'll try to get their reviewer by EOD Friday.

A couple of constraints from our customer to flag in advance:
- No outbound SSH to internet for management plane (must be routed through a bastion inside their DMZ)
- All logs must be forwarded to an on-prem SIEM with TLS mutual auth (we can provide certs)
- Patching window limited to a 4-hour overnight slot for stateful services

If you can show how the catalog maps to those constraints in the pre-read that will speed approval.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — look forward to the workshop.

Alex Turner
Sr. Platform Architect
Orchid Systems

---
